newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's 1996 IPCA-E inflation index at 9.92 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's 1996 IPCA-E inflation index at 9.92 pct.

text.p: Brazilian inflation as measured by the Special Wider National Consumers Price Index (IPCA-E) was 9.92 percent in 1996, the lowest annual rate since 1979, the National Statistics Institute (IBGE) said.
The IBGE began calculating consumer prices index in 1979, the institute said in a statement.
In 1995, inflation as measured by the IPCA-E index was 22.47 percent.
In the last quarter of 1996, the IPCA-E index was 0.75 percent.

The IPCA-E is a quarterly index based on the spending of families with an income of up to 40 minimum salaries in 11 geographical areas and is used to calculate the Ufir index which adjusts income tax.
Clothing prices registered the best results, falling 1.92 percent this year, while housing costs showed the greatest rise of 25.72 percent.
Of the 11 geographical areas, Sao Paulo showed the highest inflation with a rise of 11.72 percent, IBGE said.
The lowest inflation was seen in Belem at 6.14 percent.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom 5521 5074151))
